nations.name: Upper Mattaponi Tribe
nations.lands: King William County, Virginia; the Tribe describes its community base as within the traditional lands of Tsenacomacah

facts.text: The Tribe's history says the Upper Mattaponi were signatories to the 1677 Treaty of Middle Plantation under Cockacoeske.
facts.evidence: were signatories to the 1677 Treaty of Middle Plantation

facts.text: The Tribe's history says the Adamstown band became officially known as the Upper Mattaponi Tribe in 1921.
The Tribe's school history dates Sharon Indian School's construction to 1919.

source.title: Sharon Indian School Foundation - Upper Mattaponi Tribe

facts.text: The Tribe's school history says King William County returned Sharon Indian School to the Tribe in 1987.

source.title: Sharon Indian School Foundation - Upper Mattaponi Tribe

facts.evidence: King William County returned it to the Tribe in 1987

nations.name: Nansemond Indian Nation
nations.lands: the Nansemond River area of southeastern Virginia; the Nation describes traditional settlements extending into northeastern North Carolina

facts.text: The Nansemond Indian Nation identifies its people as Indigenous to the Nansemond River in Virginia.
facts.evidence: indigenous people of the Nansemond River

facts.text: The Nation's history describes fishing, oyster harvesting, hunting and farming in settlements on both sides of the Nansemond River.
facts.evidence: settlements on both sides of the Nansemond River

facts.text: The Nation's history dates formal organization with elected officers to 1984.
facts.evidence: formally organized with elected officers in 1984

facts.text: The Nation's published Environmental Program describes oyster restoration, invasive plant removal and native plant restoration.
facts.evidence: oyster restoration, invasive plant removal, and native plant restoration
